newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE GOVERNMENT SECURITIES END MOSTLY HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE GOVERNMENT SECURITIES END MOSTLY HIGHER.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended mostly higher in moderate trade on Friday on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.

"Government securities were mostly higher despite another fall in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.35/2.30 percent compared with Thursday's yield of 2.20/2.15 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.50.2.45 percent against 2.48/2.43 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 was unchanged from Thursday's close of S$S$98.70/98.75.
May 2002 ended at S$99.73/99.78 versus Thursday's close of S$99.70/99.75 and June 2003 at S$94.73/94.78 against S$94.70/94.75.
The overnight interbank offered rate fell to 1-1/4 1-1/8 percent from Thursday's 1-1/2 1-3/8 percent.
